recommendations.recommendation: Routine beta-blockers for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are recommended in ACS patients with HF symptoms, LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, hypertension, and/or CKD.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists are recommended in ACS patients with an LVEF ≤40% and HF or diabetes.
Routine ACE inhibitors for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered.
A polypill should be considered as an option to improve adherence and outcomes in secondary prevention after ACS.

In patients with pre-discharge LVEF ≤40%, repeat evaluation of the LVEF 6–12 weeks after an ACS (and after complete revascularization and the institution of optimal medical therapy) is recommended to assess the potential need for sudden cardiac death primary prevention ICD implantation.
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging should be considered as an adjunctive imaging modality in order to assess the potential need for primary prevention ICD implantation.
Influenza vaccination is recommended for all ACS patients.

abbreviations.ACE: angiotensin-converting enzyme (used here to name ACE inhibitors)
